title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case rather than a model error. The systems involved, a Flock camera network, a tag reader system and the Georgia Crime Information Center database, were built and licensed for police work, and the person accused of misusing them held the credentials and the training to use them legitimately. The failure sits at the point where authorised access meets no check on purpose, so the same login that supports an investigation also supports tracking a private individual.

Catching this kind of misuse requires comparing queries against a documented law enforcement justification, and reviewing that record independently of the person making the queries. The alleged conduct is described as spanning roughly three weeks, which suggests the activity was not a single anomalous lookup. The reporting does not say what audit or oversight process existed at the Coffee County Sheriff's Office, or whether any query review took place before the GBI was asked to investigate.

The charges are allegations. An indictment is not a finding of guilt, and the reporting does not establish that Rozar acted as alleged or what his intent was beyond what the charges assert. The outcome of the arraignment and any later proceedings is not established here.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A woman who says she was stalked by former Coffee County Sheriff's deputy Chris Ashley Rozar has spoken out anonymously. She hopes her story helps other women report abuse. Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts. The charges include four counts of violating his oath, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking.

Investigators allege Rozar misused the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons, not police work. The stalking charge says he followed, tracked, and surveilled a woman in Coffee County without her consent to harass and intimidate her. The alleged acts happened between April 10 and May 1, 2024. The GBI investigated after former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested it, and Rozar was fired when the investigation began. He was arrested May 5 and released on bond the same day. His arraignment is set for May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
